For each position i such that i % x == 0, if the bit at position i is set (1), we count it. Summing over all positions i satisfying i % x == 0, the number of set bits at those positions across the numbers 1..n. Equivalent to: For each bit position p (1-indexed from LSB) that is a multiple of x, count how many numbers in [1,n] have a 1 at that position. Then sum across positions p = x, 2x, 3x, ... up to some maximum (like floor(log2(n))+1 maybe). So we need to compute the total price sum S(n) = Σ_{t=1}^{⌊log2(n)⌋+1} count_ones_at_position(p=t*x) for each t such that p ≤ maxbits (position index). Actually we need all positions i where i % x == 0; i is position index starting from 1 (LSB). So these are positions x, 2x, 3x, ... .

We need to compute S(n) efficiently for given n (up to maybe something like answer could be huge because k up to 1e15, x up to 8). We can binary search on n (0..some high bound) and compute S(n). If S(n) <= k, then we can increase n, else reduce.
